processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Heating stage of the Gleeble-3500 compression schedule (shared by all deformation conditions of this alloy).
1200 °C/120 s homogenisation plateau of the schedule.
Cooled from 1200 °C to the set temperature of 1050 °C at 5 °C/s.
Held 15 s at 1050 °C so that the temperature difference between the inside and outside of the sample was the same.

processing_steps.method: isothermal constant strain rate hot compression
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Gleeble-3500 isothermal constant-strain-rate compression at 1050 °C with strain rate 10 s^-1; mica foils with high-temperature lubricants were affixed to both end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity.
After compression the sample was sprayed with water to cool the steel down (immediate quench).

structures.overall_structure: Pre-deformation (as-forged billet) microstructure: large polygonal grains delimited by a bright, continuous, slightly etched boundary network, with dark grey grain interiors containing many fine, closely spaced, parallel light-grey striations or lamellae whose direction changes from grain to grain; a strongly banded segregation contrast indicating chemical heterogeneity. Grains are large relative to the 100 µm scale bar (individual grains span roughly one to a few times the bar length).

Hot working in the range 1050-1100 °C/1-10 s^-1 (which includes this sample's condition 1050 °C/10 s^-1) yields sufficient dynamic recrystallization and a relatively fine and uniform grain structure; complete/adequate DRX rather than the insufficient DRX + retained large original grains seen at low T / high strain rate.

microstructure_list.region: large deformation zone (core of the compressed sample, where grain size is measured)

characterization_methods.technique: isothermal constant strain rate hot compression (thermo-mechanical simulation)
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator; cylindrical sample F 8 mm × 12 mm with perpendicular end faces; mica foils with high-temperature lubricants affixed to both end faces
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: T = 900-1150 °C, ε̇ = 0.01-10 s^-1; maximum compression 60% (true strain 0.92); heating rate 10 °C/s, 1200 °C/120 s homogenisation, cooling 5 °C/s, 15 s hold at set T
characterization_methods.purpose: To obtain rheological (flow) stress curves and study the hot deformation and dynamic recrystallization behaviour of the steel.
characterization_methods.key_findings: The steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain rate-sensitive material; peak stress falls with decreasing ε̇ or increasing T.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: LEXT OLS4000 laser confocal microscope; etchant = 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Compressed samples split in half along the axial axis; ground, polished and etched before imaging; 100 µm scale bars on micrographs
characterization_methods.purpose: To observe the initial and hot-deformed microstructures and the DRX grain structures in the three deformation zones.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Initial microstructure shows large polygonal grains with banded striations; after hot deformation the degree of DRX is zone 3 (large deformation) > zone 2 (small deformation) > zone 1 (difficult deformation).

computational_details.simulation_method: analytical constitutive modelling (Arrhenius hyperbolic sine + Zener-Hollomon parameter)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Activation energy derived from linear fits of the experimental peak-stress data (Fig. 4); fitted straight-line parallelism is poor, so the value is an average over the experimental range.

analytical_models.equation_role: Relates peak stress to temperature and strain rate to determine the dynamic recrystallization activation energy
Temperature-compensated strain rate Z = ε̇ exp(Qp/RT) used to characterise the combined effect of T and ε̇
analytical_models.model_note: lnZ decreases with increasing T and increases with increasing ε̇; value for 1050 °C/10 s^-1 read from Table 1.

computational_details.simulation_method: multiple linear regression of flow-stress-curve characteristic values against lnZ
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Regression correlation coefficients R: σc 0.947, εc 0.911, σp 0.957, εp 0.911, σs 0.956, εs 0.922.

analytical_models.model_name: DRX characteristic value models (εc, σc, εp, σp, εs, σs vs lnZ)
analytical_models.equation_role: Predict critical, peak and steady-state strains/stresses of DRX as functions of the Zener-Hollomon parameter

computational_details.simulation_method: Levenberg-Marquardt optimisation regression of the DRX average grain size
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Correlation coefficient R = 0.996 and MRE for all samples = 4.53%; absolute error between predicted and experimental grain size mostly within 3 µm.

analytical_models.model_name: DRX average grain size prediction model
analytical_models.equation_role: Predicts average DRX grain size from strain rate and temperature
analytical_models.model_note: Form drex = a·d0^h·ε^p·ε̇^q·exp(Q/RT) + b; initial grain size and strain taken as fixed constants.

computational_details.simulation_method: finite element simulation of hot compression
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Semi-symmetric specimen used as deformation model; billet set as rigid plastic body, die indenter as rigid body; contact friction set to shear type with value 0.3; convection coefficient between billet and air set as 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C); simulation matched the thermal-compression experimental conditions.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The simulation was in line with the experimental conditions of thermal compression.

unmapped_findings: For the exact sample condition 1050 °C / 10 s^-1 the calculated Zener-Hollomon parameter is lnZ = 63.20 (Table 1).

The paper states that sufficient dynamic recrystallization and a relatively fine and uniform grain structure can be obtained by hot working within 950-1000 °C/0.01-0.1 s^-1 and 1050-1100 °C/1-10 s^-1; this window contains the sample condition (1050 °C, 10 s^-1).
The steel is reported as a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material: flow stress increases with increasing strain rate or decreasing temperature.
The average dynamic recrystallization activation energy of the steel is 669.844 kJ mol^-1.

The DRX grain-size prediction model for the steel has a correlation coefficient R = 0.996, MRE = 4.53% for all samples, with predicted-vs-experimental absolute error generally below 3 µm (one point near ~4.2 µm).

No separate micrograph or numeric average grain size is reported for the exact 1050 °C/10 s^-1 condition: the Fig. 9 panel set covers 1050 °C only at ε̇ = 1 s^-1 and 1100 °C for the strain-rate series (0.01, 0.1, 10 s^-1).
